To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the uncertainty of the POArear irradiance measurement can be reduced by using a reference cell, by placing the sensors at the same height as the panels and by using a pyranometer with a large field of view.

the uncertainty of the backside irradiace measurement is strongly affected by the installation position of the sensors with respect to the panel height. The closer the sensors are to the panel, the higher the backside irradiation.

the uncertainty of irradiance measurements on the backside of PV panels depends on the sensor position with respect to the panel height and that the uncertainty is larger for sensors placed higher on the panel than on the ground, especially for sensors with small field of view.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How much uncertainty is introduced by the installation position of sensors? How much uncertainty is added by the use of experimental pyranometers?
the following aspects: • Uncertainties in POArear measurement of bifacial solar modules with different measurement technologies.
the following questions: (1) What are the main factors affecting backside irradiance measurements?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is still no standard method for measuring the POArear irradiance.

the POArear irradiance is difficult to measure accurately and that the uncertainty is strongly influenced by several factors, such as the type of measurement device, the installation position, the panel height, and the tilt angle.
the uncertainty of POArear irradiance measurement strongly depends on the measurement technology, its installation position, panel orientation and albedo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the irradiance measurements of POArear are not as straightforward as for the front side, but can be performed with sufficient accuracy for PV performance ratio analysis.
the uncertainty of the POArear irradiance measurements is strongly dependent on the installation height of the sensors.
the POArear uncertainty is mainly caused by the measurement technology and the installation position with respect, to the panel height.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of POArear is challenging and the uncertainty of POArear measurements is high.
POArear irradiance is highly dependent on the albedo, the angle of incidence of the irradiance on the back of the panel, and the position of the measurement device with respect to the panel height.
POArear measurements are very sensitive to the position of the sensor with respect to panel tilt.
